transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I suppose I’m here because... well, it’s a long story, but the short version is that for nearly two years now, I’ve been absolutely certain—and I mean completely sure, despite what anyone else says—that the contractor we hired for our kitchen remodel and some of the people living on my block have been quietly working together. It’s not just a feeling; it’s a coordinated effort to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. 

I mean, it all started back when we first decided to update the cabinets, and then one thing led to another, and suddenly the plumbing is off, the tile is crooked, and I see the contractor talking to the Johnsons across the street. And my husband, bless his heart, he keeps showing me all these receipts and invoices, trying to prove everything is above board. He says, "Look, Martha, here’s the breakdown of the costs," but he just doesn't see the bigger picture. And the excuses! Oh, the excuses they give me. "Supply chain issues," they say, or "We had to wait for the inspector." But I know what’s really going on. They’re dragging it out, doing it poorly on purpose, and no matter how many times they try to explain it away or how many pieces of paper my husband waves in my face, I know they’re all in on it together. It’s just exhausting, frankly, having to be the only one who sees it.
That sounds very stressful for you. During this time, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people didn't seem to hear?

Voices? Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, my hearing is perfectly fine—well, maybe a little ringing sometimes if my husband leaves the television volume up too high on his news programs, but that’s just normal, you know? I’m 67, not 90! I don’t need a hearing aid, and I certainly don't hear... invisible people talking, if that's what you're getting at. I know some people have those sorts of troubles, but my mind is as sharp as a tack. 

The things I hear are very, very real. Just last Tuesday, for instance, I was standing by the front bay window—the one that looks right out onto the street, right over where my prize hydrangeas are planted—and I heard the contractor and Mr. Johnson. Clear as day! Well, they were whispering, trying to keep it all hushed and secretive, but I could hear the tone of it. They were standing right by that rusted old truck the contractor drives, muttering to each other, looking at my house. So no, I don't hear imaginary voices. I hear actual, real-life conversations that they think I’m too oblivious to notice. 

And my husband, he'll sit there in his recliner and say, "Martha, you couldn't possibly hear what they're saying from inside the house," but he's missing the point! It’s the way they lower their voices the second I step out onto the porch to get the mail. They stop talking completely, or they start talking about the weather, real loud and fake. That’s what I hear. The sneaky hushed tones. Not made-up sounds in my head, just the very real way people behave when they think you aren't paying attention to their little games.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions, or had any major physical illnesses around the time this all started?

Medical conditions? Oh, no. No, I’m quite healthy, thank the Lord. I mean, I’ve always been very careful about taking care of myself, you know? I take my vitamins—a good multivitamin, calcium for the bones because, well, at my age, you have to be sensible about these things. And I walk every evening. My husband and I, we used to walk down to the park, but lately, with all this business going on with the neighbors, I prefer to just walk on the treadmill in the basement. It’s safer, and I don't have to worry about who is watching me from their front porches. 

But as for major illnesses? Neurological things? Absolutely not. My doctor, Dr. Evans—he’s been my general practitioner for, oh, it must be fifteen years now—he always says my blood pressure is perfect. "Like a teenager," he tells me, which is very sweet of him, even if it's an exaggeration. I haven't had so much as a bad flu in years. I certainly haven't had any strokes or head injuries or whatever it is that causes people to lose their faculties. My mind is perfectly sound. 

It’s actually very frustrating, you know, because my husband will sometimes hint at things like that. He’ll say, "Martha, maybe you’re just tired, maybe we should have your thyroid checked again," as if a thyroid problem could possibly explain why the contractor ordered the wrong color grout for the backsplash three separate times! It’s insulting, frankly. They try to make it seem like there's something wrong with *me*, physically, to distract from what they are doing. But I know my own body, and I know my own mind. I am perfectly healthy. There was no illness, no sudden medical crisis. Just the sudden realization that these people were taking advantage of us, right under our noses.
